To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a cluster of ARE-mRNas that is upregulated in cancer.
the balance in the expression levels of the ARE-mRNA binding proteins, TTP and Hu, is reversed in cancer.

1) A set of AU-rich element (ARE)-mRNAs that are regulated by TTP and Hu are significantly overrepresented in cancer, and that 2) the overexpression of these ARE-mRNAs in cancer is associated with poor patient survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
posttranscriptional mechanisms that regulate gene expression and are important for the pathogenesis of cancer.
a novel mechanism of cancer development and progression, which involves the post-transcriptional regulation of mitotic genes via the ARE-mRNA signature and its regulation by TTP/Hu.
the role of AU-rich elements (AU-Rich Element) (AREs), RNA-binding motifs that regulate posttranslational control, in cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AREs are overexpressed in multiple cancers, and the expression of AREs is regulated by TTP/HuRs.

TTP and HuD are two key RNA-binding proteins that control the expression of a large set of ARE-containing mRNAs that are involved in the mitosis process and are over-represented and dysregulated in a number cancer types.
the expression of ARE-mRNas is significantly associated with cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a cluster of mitotic cell cycle-related genes that were upregulated by the loss of TTP and the gain of HuR in cancer.
we identified a cluster of ARE-mRNas (CDC6, PRC1 and NEK2) that negatively correlated to TTP and Hu R and was upregulated in cancer.
the ARE-mRNas are involved in cancer, and that the TTP/Hu ratio is an important determinant of the outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RNA-binding protein TTP induces a mitotic cell-cycle block that is lost in cancer.
TTP is a tumor suppressor that is diminished in many cancers.
TTP and Hu-R are key regulators of post-transcriptional gene expression in cancer and that TTP is involved in the control of mitotic cell-cycle genes.
